newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC sees 0.5-pct Swiss growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: SBC sees 0.5-pct Swiss growth in 1997.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) forecasts the Swiss economy to expand by about 0.5 percent in 1997, fuelled by export growth estimated at 3.9 percent and a rise in capital investment of between eight and nine percent.

However, the bank said in a quarterly economic report that the outlook for the domestic building sector was bleak for about the next 18 months, given the current state of the domestic property market.
SBC also forecasts gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 2.0 percent in 1998.
It said the price decline in the apartment rental sector was levelling off, but prices still have not reached bottom.
The outlook for single family homes and condominiums was somewhat better. But prices in the commecial property sector are continuing to sink parallel to declining demand.
The International Monetary Fund recently predicted real GDP growth of around 1.0 percent for 1997 after an estimated 0.5-percent contraction in 1996. -- Zurich Editorial +41 631 7340
